title: High-resolution multichannel seismic-reflection profiles across the Helena Banks strike-slip fault zone offshore of the Charleston, South Carolina, earthquake area
citation: Yuan, Annette, and Behrendt, J.C., 1988, High-resolution multichannel seismic-reflection profiles across the Helena Banks strike-slip fault zone offshore of the Charleston, South Carolina, earthquake area: U.S. Geological Survey Miscellaneous Field Studies Map MF-2056, map scale 1:740,000.
notes:
Single OCR plate: text, trackline map (fig. 1), seismic sections (figs. 2-4). Seismic record sections OCR as noise; nothing read from them. Fault data from the text and figure captions; Cretaceous and Triassic(?) faults and epicenters known only from the fig. 1 explanation not recorded. References: South Carolina items recorded; general margin-wide references (Behrendt and Grim 1983, Behrendt and Klitgord 1979, Dillon and others 1979, Grow and others 1979, Klitgord and Behrendt 1977, 1979, Zoback and others 1986) skipped. OCR typos in citations ('Tectonies', 'Seismie') corrected in values only.
SUBSURFACE: J reflection (top of Jurassic basalt under Upper Cretaceous sediments) lies at 0.8-1.2 s two-way traveltime across the survey area; schema elevation fields need ft or m, so it is not stored as a surface (the text gives 1 s ~ 1 km for the upper second, at 2.0 km/s). Seismic sections are in two-way time with no depth or elevation datum. Water depth about 20 m in the fault zone.
